subject: english
question: What is the subject of a sentence?
options: The person or thing the sentence is about
The full stop at the end
The action word in the sentence
The describing word in the sentence
hint: The subject is who or what the sentence is about. Ask “who?” or “what?” before the verb.

subject: english
question: What is the predicate of a sentence?
options: The question mark or full stop
The first word of the sentence
Everything that tells you what the subject does or is
hint: The predicate is the rest of the sentence — the verb and everything that goes with it.

subject: english
question: Every complete sentence must have which two parts?
options: A capital letter and a comma
hint: Without a subject you do not know who; without a predicate you do not know what happened.

subject: english
question:
What is the SUBJECT of this sentence?

“The Giant came back.”
hint: Ask who or what the sentence is about: The Giant. The rest tells you what they did.

subject: english
question:
What is the PREDICATE of this sentence?

“The Giant came back.”
hint: The predicate is everything that says what the subject does — “came back”.

question: In “Under the tree sat a very small boy”, what is the subject?
hint: The sentence is turned around, but it is still about the boy. Ask who sat — the boy did.

subject: english
question: Which of these is NOT a complete sentence?
options: The Giant knocked down the wall
Ran away through the hole in the wall
Spring came back to the garden
hint: It has a predicate but no subject — you are never told who ran. That makes it a fragment.

subject: english
question: Which of these is NOT a complete sentence?
options: The Hail rattled on the roof
A high wall all round the garden
The boy could not reach the branches
The frost painted the trees silver
hint: It names a thing but never says what it did or was. There is no predicate.

subject: english
question: In “The Giant’s garden was very beautiful”, what is the predicate?
hint: A predicate does not have to be an action. Here it tells you what the subject WAS.

subject: english
question: A subject can be more than one word. Which is the full subject of “The tall grey wall hid the garden”?
hint: The full subject includes the words that describe it — all of “The tall grey wall”.

subject: english
question: What does subject–verb agreement mean?
options: The verb must always end in -ing
The verb must match the subject in number — singular or plural
The subject must always come before the verb
The subject and the verb must rhyme
hint: One child plays; two children play. The verb changes to match how many.

subject: english
question: With a SINGULAR subject in the present tense, what usually happens to the verb?
options: It takes an -s: the boy plays
It loses its -s: the boy play
hint: Oddly, it is the verb that takes the -s when the subject is singular: he plays, they play.

subject: english

“The Giant ___ in a great castle.”
hint: The Giant is one, so the verb takes an -s.

question:

hint: Children is plural, so the verb has no -s.

subject: english
question: Which sentence is CORRECT?
options: The children were playing in the garden.
The children is playing in the garden.
The children was playing in the garden.
The children has playing in the garden.
hint: Children is plural, so it takes were.

subject: english
question: Which sentence is CORRECT?
options: The Giant having a beautiful garden.
The Giant has a beautiful garden.
The Giant have a beautiful garden.
The Giant are having beautiful garden.
hint: One Giant — has. Have goes with plural subjects and with I and you.

subject: english
question: Which sentence is WRONG?
options: The tree in the garden was bare.
The trees in the garden was bare.
The trees in the garden were bare.
hint: The subject is trees, which is plural, so it needs were. The words in the garden sit between them and are easy to be misled by.

subject: english
question: “The sound of the children ___ lovely.” Which verb is right?
hint: The subject is sound, not children. One sound — was. This is the trap of a phrase coming between subject and verb.

subject: english
question: Why is “The list of words are long” wrong?
options: The subject is list, which is singular, so it needs is
hint: Of words describes the list. The list itself is one thing, so the verb is is.
